newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end sharply higher on export talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end sharply higher on export talk.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended sharply higher, led by old crop on rumors of export business in the works, pit sources said.
"With the kind of beating the soybeans have taken we have now priced ourselves comparably to South America," said Dave Maher, analyst with Securities Corp of Iowa.

Rumors were rampant that China bought U.S. old and new crop soybeans. There was also talk of old crop supplies sold to Europe and that Brazilian crushers were looking for U.S. soybeans. U.S. exporters could not confirm the rumors but said it was unlikely Brazil or China would buy old crop.

Some traders said it was logical Europe would buy old crop soybeans, possibly out of the U.S. Great Lakes. Soybeans FOB Great Lakes were $267.10 a tonne FOB while Brazilian beans FOB Paranagua were at $282.90, export sources said.
July soybeans surged on ideas there would be no deliveries posted against the July. Two commercial firms lifted short positions on Monday, a move traders said lessened the likelihood of delivery.
Soybeans ended 35-1/4 to 9-1/2 cents per bushel higher with July up 35-1/4 at $7.68 and new crop November up 9-1/2 at $5.93-3/4.
Funds bought at least 19 million bushels November on the day which boosted new crop months. Trade sources pointed to signals the market was oversold and to old crop/new crop spread alignments.
The November contract has shed roughly 50 cents a bushel since June 30 when the USDA said farmers planted 70.85 million acres of soybeans this year.

That makes this the third largest planted area on record. Growing conditions were said to be ideal, leading to calls for 2.8 billion to 2.9 billion bushels of soybeans. The record crop of 1994 was roughly 2.5 billion bushels.

Weather patterns were deemed conducive to crop development and conditions continued to improve. USDA on Monday said 68 percent of the U.S. soybean crop was in good to excellent condition, up from 65 percent last week.

On the day, funds were aggressive buyers of the November, led by Refco Inc. Refco bought at least eight million bushels November, Tenco Inc bought four million August and one million November, and Term Commodities bought two million August and 1.5 million November.
In options trade, CIS sold 700 August $7.25 puts at 19 to 26 cents, CIS also sold 400 September $6.50 puts at 36 cents and 400 August $8.00 calls at 2-1/2 cents.
Volatility in the August jumped to 35-3/4 percent from 30-1/2 percent on Monday. The November closed at 20 percent from 19-3/4 on Monday.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 63,000 contracts, above Monday's actual volume of 52,393 contracts. Options volume was pegged at 30,000 contracts, against Monday's 29,435
